products.name: Twelve Hours' Sleep by Twelve Weeks Old: A Step-by-Step Plan for Baby Sleep Success

reviews.content:
I read this book and then threw it in the trash. What the author is suggesting is neglectful and biologically at odds with a child's needs. Scheduled feedings have been linked to failure to thrive in infants and I've never heard of a doctor who suggested that a child sleep for more than a 5 hour stretch by 12 weeks of age!

I'll read Dr. Sears next time. His advice is helpful and not DANGEROUS!
reviews.title: Garbage

reviews.content: I'm buying this book for a friend having a baby because everyone I know that read it and followed it had success sleep training their babies. My son slept 12 hours by 10 weeks old and it's a game changer. We credit this book entirely.
reviews.title: Amazing book

reviews.content: I used this book to sleep train all 3 of my kids and it helped amazingly. Short simple steps written in a concise and understandable manner makes it easy for any parent to follow. Just have to follow all her basic instructions and keep consistent to get results. I’ve referred it to countless friends who it has worked for as well.

reviews.content: I love this book. You don't need to take the entire thing as gospel but take the tips and work with them. Some of the reviews below are too harsh. The author isn't suggesting you starve your baby for 4 hours or completely leave them for 12 hours but the fundamentals are there for a great development of habits for the child. I have 2 kids and this worked for me on both. One was smaller and slept though the night at 13 weeks and the other much much bigger slept through the night at 9 weeks. So like i said, no need to take the entire thing as gospel but there are alot of good tips in there to use in your role of helping your child soothe themselves and learn to sleep on their own. All should be done in a loving, nurturing way.
reviews.title: Don't the bad reviews too seriously, this book has some great tips.
